question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose an optional runtime-local reset-correlation token on the shared agent-harness reset parameters and plugin `session_end` event so plugins can safely correlate a successful reset with its delayed lifecycle end?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but deciding whether this correlation belongs in the generic lifecycle API or must remain Codex-owned determines the compatibility contract for future harnesses and plugins.

options.title: Accept the generic lifecycle correlation
options.body: Keep `resetToken` optional and document it as a one-shot, runtime-local correlation field for successful reset hooks and their matching delayed session-end events.

options.title: Use a Codex-owned correlation seam
options.body: Redesign the handoff so the Codex plugin preserves the same fail-closed behavior without extending the shared harness and plugin lifecycle contracts.

recommendation.title: Accept the generic lifecycle correlation
recommendation.body: Keep `resetToken` optional and document it as a one-shot, runtime-local correlation field for successful reset hooks and their matching delayed session-end events.

likelyOwner.reason: The durable retained-session reset model that this PR completes was introduced in the merged reset work.
